content:
**Fixed the unreadable issue body substitute in brain:snapshot**

What: readForge in brain/scripts/status/snapshot.mjs caught a failed vcs.issueView and substituted an empty body, so the node built from it was byte-identical to an issue that declared no graph block (declared:false, status:unclassified). The node now carries ok:false, the reason, status:unreadable, declared:null, and is listed in graph.issuesUnreadable; the tracks object omits it instead of placing it under the ? track. Why: cold review of PR #953 rev 1, blocker judgment:cold-1, citing brain/core/anti-patterns/evidence-reader-empty-on-failure.md and spec rule R879-2. Where: brain/scripts/status/snapshot.mjs, brain/scripts/status/snapshot.test.mjs, openspec/changes/issue-879-snapshot-read-model/{spec,design}.md. Learned: the pre-existing test fed issueView an empty body for the undeclared case and its assertions would also have passed on the failure substitute; it now pins ok:true and issuesUnreadable:[] so the two adjacent tests differ. Mutation check: catch reverted to an empty body turns exactly the unreadable test red (ok expected false, actual true), the other ten stay green. A cold review run seconds after a push, while gates were pending, posted an empty-bodied review on b77b5254 (issue #945), so the head had to move.
